title: Fine-Grained Analysis of Catastrophic Forgetting in Continual Learning via Algorithmic Stability
abstract: arXiv:2610.31551v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Understanding catastrophic forgetting, in which learning new tasks degrades performance on previously learned tasks, remains a fundamental challenge in continual learning (CL). Existing theoretical analyses often rely on specific model or task structures and offer limited insight into how iterative optimization affects forgetting. To address this gap, we develop an algorithmic stability framework for expected population forgetting under SGD without prescribing a particular model architecture. Specifically, we decompose forgetting into intra-task and cross-task generalization gaps and empirical forgetting. To bound the generalization gaps, we track how a sample perturbation affects updates within a task and propagates through subsequent tasks. We consider constant, intra-task decaying, and continuously decaying learning-rate schedules. Comparing the two decaying schedules allows us to characterize how restarting learning-rate decay at tas

translated_title: 通过算法稳定性对持续学习中灾难性遗忘的细粒度分析
translated_abstract: 理解灾难性遗忘——即学习新任务会导致在先前已学习任务上的性能下降——仍然是持续学习（CL）中的一个基本挑战。现有的理论分析通常依赖于特定的模型或任务结构，对于迭代优化如何影响遗忘所提供的洞察有限。为了填补这一空白，我们开发了一个算法稳定性框架，用于分析SGD下的期望总体遗忘，而无需指定特定的模型架构。具体而言，我们将遗忘分解为任务内和跨任务的泛化差距以及经验遗忘。为了界定泛化差距，我们追踪样本扰动如何影响任务内的更新并在后续任务中传播。我们考虑了恒定学习率、任务内衰减学习率和持续衰减学习率三种调度方式。比较两种衰减调度方式使我们能够刻画在任务开始时重新启动学习率衰减如何影响遗忘（摘要在此处被截断）。
tldr: 本文提出了一个不依赖特定模型架构的算法稳定性理论框架，将持续学习中的灾难性遗忘细粒度地分解为任务内与跨任务泛化差距及经验遗忘，并系统分析了三种学习率调度对遗忘的影响。
en_tdlr: This paper develops an algorithmic stability framework for expected population forgetting under SGD without prescribing a particular model architecture, providing a fine-grained decomposition of catastrophic forgetting into intra-task and cross-task generalization gaps and empirical forgetting, and characterizing the effects of different learning-rate schedules on forgetting.
